newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - IPE Brent seeks recent $18.32 high.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - IPE Brent seeks recent $18.32 high.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
+ A bear island reversal pattern formed last week remains intact but a firm close on Monday has set the stage for an attack on the initial resistance level at around $18.00.
+ The top of this island reversal pattern lies at $18.32 and this is the next upside target.
IPE Brent crude oil futures are still in a consolidative pattern on Tuesday although a strong close on Monday has set the stage for some recovery, traders said.
August Brent closed 31 cents firmer on Monday at $17.98 a barrel, while July gas oil ended $1.75 a tonne up at $160.25.
"The action is still consolidative," said Steve Kwan at MMS in London. "This could be a minor base-forming pattern as we are seeing a positive momentum picture."

Brent was trading in Singapore above $18.00 ahead of the IPE market's open. A move into this territory in London would negate the initial resistance formed by last week's bear island reversal pattern at $18.02.
"I expect a retest of $18.32," said Kwan, referring to the high point reached at the top of the reversal pattern.
Above that level, he said, the next resistance would be found at $18.70.
A move below current levels would find support at $17.60-$17.70, corresponding to recent lows.

Peter Sceats at CharTech-MCS said in a weekly report released on Monday said that in addition to last week's bear island reversal, the break last week of the previous low at $17.54 "can be said to set the market up for later losses."
The weekly chart, too, was looking weak, he added.
"As so often happened support has turned into resistance. Last week's high was right on the underside of the old up trend."
"The 'trough failure' (a break of $17.54) is added to the 'peak failure' (failure to top $20.84). The downside target has to be $17.32," he said.
But he added: "Watch the 14- and 22-day stochastics closely. They are the bullish caveat to a mostly bearish Brent market.
Gas oil will find support first at $160.00 and then at $158.00 a tonne, the lowest point reached on the continuation chart since last year.
